memory_update.text: LRN should remain the reference anchor for virtual K-12 and career-learning platforms, but later layers should avoid letting it crowd out infrastructure suppliers.
NNI is a high-priority underfollowed candidate because FACTS/NBS may provide the administrative and payments infrastructure layer for K-12 private, faith-based, and alternative schools.
LOPE belongs in the adjacent workforce-learning lane, with focus on employer-originated starts, online enrollment, licensure fields, and hybrid healthcare education.
UTI belongs in the career-learning lane as a small-cap workforce-training operator tied to skilled trades and healthcare education rather than conventional online K-12.

The most defensible chokepoints for this node appear to be authorization, state/district or school relationships, employer relationships, student-support operations, payment/admin infrastructure, licensure-aligned curriculum, and measurable outcomes.

Need a later pass on curriculum, assessment, tutoring, teacher staffing, special education, and learning-management suppliers; this pass found NNI as the clearest hidden K-12 infrastructure name but did not exhaust the supplier universe.

node: Virtual K-12, alternative schooling, and career-learning platforms
summary: Expanded the node from pure-play online K-12 operators into adjacent career-learning, education services, school-management infrastructure, payments, and workforce-aligned postsecondary platforms. Stride is the reference anchor, but the underfollowed lane is more interesting in Nelnet's FACTS K-12 infrastructure, Grand Canyon Education's employer/university service model, and Universal Technical Institute's skilled-trades/healthcare career-training platform. The chokepoint hypothesis remains that authorization, curriculum breadth, student support, school/district workflows, employer relationships, and outcome credibility may matter more than generic video-course delivery.
